children.text: After 4 weeks the results can be seen with the people who did not use their phones 30 minutes before bed reducing the time it takes them to fall asleep by 12 minutes. The duration of their sleep increased by 18 minutes. Measures of sleep quality also were seen to have improved.
Discussion of Pre-sleep arousal and how the sensations experienced by phone usage right before bed lead to people finding it harder to fall asleep. This reduced when the phone usage reduced.
Moods improved whilst functiionality indicators like reaction time and memory were also seen to have improved. Links sleep to cognitive function.
Potential limitations of the study, small sample size. Discusses blue light effects on sleep.
